claims.source: One model suggests that a decrease in histone levels over time due to dilution during nuclear division provides an opportunity for the pioneer factors that drive zygotic gene expression to successfully compete for DNA access and activate transcription (Shindo and Amodeo, 2019; Hamm and Harrison, 2018).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work proposing this model.

claims.claim: Zld increases accessibility of chromatin at enhancers thereby allowing binding of other transcriptional activators.
claims.source: For example, Zld is pivotal for the MZT as it increases accessibility of chromatin at enhancers thereby allowing binding of other transcriptional activators at these DNA regions which facilitates initiation of zygotic gene expression (Xu et al., 2014; Harrison et al., 2011; Liang et al., 2008; Nien et al., 2011; Yáñez-Cuna et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work on Zelda's function.

claims.claim: Zld binds nucleosomes, a characteristic of pioneer factors.
claims.source: Zld binds nucleosomes, another characteristic of pioneer factors (McDaniel et al., 2019), and therefore loss of Zld leads to a global decrease in zygotic gene expression as many enhancer regions remain inaccessible (Schulz et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Loss of Zld leads to a global decrease in zygotic gene expression as many enhancer regions remain inaccessible.
claims.source: Zld binds nucleosomes, another characteristic of pioneer factors (McDaniel et al., 2019), and therefore loss of Zld leads to a global decrease in zygotic gene expression as many enhancer regions remain inaccessible (Schulz et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Zld influences the ability of morphogen transcription factors, Bicoid and Dorsal, to support embryonic patterning.
claims.source: Through its effects on chromatin accessibility, Zld has been shown to influence the ability of morphogen transcription factors, Bicoid and Dorsal, to support embryonic patterning (Xu et al., 2014; Foo et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Some genes continue to be expressed even in the absence of Zld.
claims.source: While Zld is clearly pivotal for supporting MZT, some genes continue to be expressed even in its absence (Nien et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Chromatin accessibility in the early embryo is a dynamic process.
claims.source: As chromatin accessibility in the early embryo has recently been shown to be a dynamic process (Blythe and Wieschaus, 2016b; Bozek et al., 2019), it is possible that Zld contributes in a stage-specific manner and that other as yet unidentified pioneer factors contribute to the extended process of zygotic genome activation.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: The midblastula transition (MBT) is marked by dramatic slowing of the division cycle and cellularization of nuclei.
claims.source: The embryo undergoes a widespread state change after the 14th nuclear division, termed the midblastula transition (MBT) (Foe and Alberts, 1983; Shermoen et al., 2010). This developmental milestone is marked by dramatic slowing of the division cycle and cellularization of nuclei before the onset of embryonic programs of morphogenesis and differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work defining MBT.

claims.claim: At nc14, developmental changes relating to DNA replication occur, including a lengthened S-phase and the introduction of G2 phase into the cell cycle.
claims.source: In addition, at nc14, developmental changes relating to DNA replication occur; namely a lengthened S-phase and the introduction of G2 phase into the cell cycle.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing changes at nc14.

claims.claim: MBT is associated with clearance of a subset of maternally provided mRNAs, large-scale transcriptional activation of the zygotic genome, and an increase in cell cycle length.
claims.source: MBT is also associated with clearance of a subset of maternally provided mRNAs, large-scale transcriptional activation of the zygotic genome, and an increase in cell cycle length (Yuan et al., 2016; Tadros and Lipshitz, 2009).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Odd-paired (opa) encodes the founding member of the Zinc finger in the cerebellum (Zic) protein family.
claims.source: The Drosophila gene odd-paired (opa) encodes the founding member of the Zinc finger in the cerebellum (Zic) protein family (Aruga et al., 1996; Hursh and Stultz, 2018).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Zic (ZIC human ortholog) plays an important regulatory role in early developmental processes across major animal models and is implicated in human pathology.
claims.source: The important regulatory role of Zic (ZIC human ortholog) in early developmental processes has been established across major animal models and also implicated in human pathology (rev. in Aruga and Millen, 2018; Houtmeyers et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to review articles.

claims.claim: opa is activated during mid-nc14.
claims.source: opa is a broadly expressed gene of relatively long transcript length (~17 kB) that is activated during mid-nc14 and serves a number of important functions throughout development (Cimbora and Sakonju, 1995; Benedyk et al., 1994).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa protein has a DNA-binding domain containing five Cys2His2-type zinc fingers.
claims.source: Opa protein has a DNA-binding domain containing five Cys2His2-type zinc fingers, and shares homology with mammalian Zic1, 2, and three transcription factors.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing Opa protein structure.

claims.claim: opa mutants exhibit a pair-rule phenotype.
claims.source: While mutants exhibit a pair-rule phenotype (Jürgens et al., 1984), the broad expression pattern of opa contrasts with the typical 7-stripe pattern of other pair-rule genes.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa acts as a timing factor to broadly regulate the expression of segment polarity genes including the transition of pair-rule genes to segmental expression patterns.
claims.source: Rather than providing spatial information as do most other pair-rule transcription factors, Opa instead acts as a timing factor to broadly regulate the expression of segment polarity genes including the transition of pair-rule genes to segmental expression patterns (i.e. from 7- to 14-stripes) (Clark and Akam, 2016; Benedyk et al., 1994).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: opa mutant embryos die before hatching and exhibit defects in larval midgut formation in addition to aberrant segmentation.
claims.source: opa mutant embryos die before hatching and in addition to aberrant segmentation, they also exhibit defects in larval midgut formation (Cimbora and Sakonju, 1995).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: During midgut formation, Opa regulates expression of a pivotal receptor tyrosine kinase required for proper morphogenesis of the visceral mesoderm.
claims.source: During midgut formation, Opa regulates expression of a pivotal receptor tyrosine kinase required for proper morphogenesis of the visceral mesoderm (Mendoza-García et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa supports temporal patterning of intermediate neural progenitors of the Drosophila larval brain at later stages.
claims.source: In addition, at later stages, Opa supports temporal patterning of intermediate neural progenitors of the Drosophila larval brain (Abdusselamoglu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa can influence the activity of other transcription factors to promote gene expression.
claims.source: Previous studies suggested that Opa can influence the activity of other transcription factors to promote gene expression.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a summary of prior work.

claims.claim: sloppy-paired 1 (slp1) is a well-characterized target of Opa in the early embryo.
claims.source: A well-characterized target of Opa in the early embryo is sloppy-paired 1 (slp1), a gene exhibiting a segment polarity expression pattern and for which two distinct enhancers have been identified that are capable of responding to regulation by Opa and other pair-rule transcription factors including Runt (Run; Cadigan et al., 1994; Prazak et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa plays a central role in supporting Run's activating input at the slp1 DESE enhancer.
claims.source: One of these, the slp1 DESE enhancer, mediates both Run-dependent repression and activation and Opa plays a central role by supporting Run's activating input (Hang and Gergen, 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Run regulates the spatiotemporal response of the sog_Distal enhancer to support its expression in a broad stripe across the dorsal-ventral axis.
claims.source: Additionally, our recent study showed that Run regulates the spatiotemporal response of another enhancer, sog_Distal (Ozdemir et al., 2011; also known as sog_Shadow; Hong et al., 2008) to support its expression in a broad stripe across the dorsal-ventral (DV) axis on both sides of the embryo (Koromila and Stathopoulos, 2019).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work including the authors' own recent study.

claims.claim: Run's role changes from repressor to activator over time in the context of sog_Distal.
claims.source: Using a combination of fixed and live imaging approaches, our analysis suggested that Run's role changes from repressor to activator over time in the context of sog_Distal; late expression requires Run activating input.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction summarizing findings from the authors' recent study.

claims.claim: The sog_Distal 650 bp enhancer sequence contains five putative 12 bp Opa binding sites based on comparison with the vertebrate Zic3 consensus motif.
claims.source: In concordance with this hypothesis, the sog Distal 650 bp enhancer sequence contains five putative 12 bp Opa binding sites, based on comparison with the vertebrate Zic3 consensus motif (JASPAR; Figure 1I).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1I.

claims.claim: Mutation of five Opa binding sites in sog_Distal (sogD_ΔOpa) results in greatly reduced expression at nc14C compared to wildtype.
claims.source: Quantitative analysis of MS2-MCP signal in embryos containing either the wildtype sog_Distal or sogD_ΔOpa reporters using a previously described analysis pipeline (Koromila and Stathopoulos, 2019) confirms that sog_Distal expression is greatly reduced at nc14C for the mutant reporter compared to wildtype (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: Mutation of even a single Opa site results in loss of late expression only (nc14C onwards) comparable to when the Run site is mutated.
claims.source: A similar loss of late expression only (i.e. nc14C onwards) was observed when even a single Opa site is mutated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, B', E) and this decrease is comparable to when the Run site is mutated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, D; Koromila and Stathopoulos, 2019).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Opa promotes expression through sog_Distal from nc14C onwards, possibly by supporting Run's switch from repressor to activator.
claims.source: These results support the view that Opa promotes expression through sog_Distal from nc14C onwards, possibly, by supporting Run's switch from repressor to activator (see Discussion).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the mutant reporter data.

claims.claim: Opa expression is absent at nc13, first observed at nc14B, and achieves its mature pattern approximately by nc14C.
claims.source: Opa expression is absent at nc13, first observed at nc14B, and achieves its mature pattern approximately by nc14C (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by anti-Opa antibody staining shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: The timing of Opa onset of expression correlates with the timing of loss of late expression from the sog_Distal reporter when Opa sites are mutated.
claims.source: The timing of Opa onset of expression correlates with the timing of loss of late expression from the sog_Distal reporter observed when Opa sites are mutated (i.e. sogD_ΔOpa; Figure 1D, compare with 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section comparing Opa expression timing with mutant reporter phenotype.

claims.claim: The ubiquitous, maternal transcription factor Zld is detected throughout nc13 and nc14.
claims.source: On the other hand, the ubiquitous, maternal transcription factor Zld is detected throughout this time period including during nc13 (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by anti-Zld antibody staining shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Loss of Zld input to sog_Distal through mutation of Zld binding sites leads to spatial retraction of the reporter pattern rather than an overall loss of expression.
claims.source: Loss of Zld input to sog_Distal through mutation of Zld binding sites leads to spatial retraction of the reporter pattern (sog_Shadow; Yamada et al., 2019) rather than an overall loss of expression as observed when Opa-binding sites are mutated (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section comparing effects of Zld versus Opa site mutations, with citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa ChIP-seq at 3 hr identified 16,085 peaks representing genomic positions occupied by Opa in vivo.
claims.source: For the 3 hr ChIP-seq dataset, the MACS2 peak caller was used to identify 16,085 peaks, providing an estimate of the number of genomic positions occupied by Opa in vivo at this developmental timepoint.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing ChIP-seq analysis.

claims.claim: The most significant motif identified in Opa 3 hr ChIP-seq peaks is a 7 bp core sequence with homology to the 12 bp Opa JASPAR consensus and mammalian Zic transcription factors.
claims.source: The most significant hit, present in over 19% of all peaks, is a 7 bp core sequence with homology to the 12 bp Opa JASPAR consensus (Figure 1J, compare with 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 2) as well as to mammalian homolog Zic transcription factors (e.g. see Figure 1I; Lim et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing motif analysis of ChIP-seq data, with reference to figures.

claims.claim: Opa ChIP-seq detects Opa occupancy at sog_Distal during the 3 hr but not the 4 hr window.
claims.source: Opa ChIP-seq detects Opa occupancy at sog_Distal during the 3 hr but not the 4 hr window (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1F genome browser tracks.

claims.claim: Opa (3 hr) and Opa (4 hr) ChIP-seq experiments each identified ~16K peaks with 9995 peaks in common.
claims.source: Opa (3 hr) and Opa (4 hr) ChIP-seq experiments each identified ~16K peaks of occupancy representing locations in the genome that are occupied by Opa, with 9995 peaks in common (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Approximately 6K peaks are occupied by Opa early-only (nc14) and a roughly equal number are occupied late-only (following gastrulation, stage 6–8).
claims.source: This suggests that ~6K peaks are occupied early-only (i.e. nc14; including late nc14 when enhancers associated with segmentation are active) and a roughly equal number are occupied late-only (following gastrulation, stage 6–8) possibly relating to Opa's transition to a role in supporting visceral mesoderm specification (Mendoza-García et al., 2017) or other roles.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the overlap between Opa 3 hr and 4 hr ChIP-seq peaks.

claims.claim: For Opa 3 hr and Zld nc13-14 comparison, 6087 peaks are in common (Opa-Zld overlap), 9998 regions are bound by Opa alone (Opa-only), and 10781 regions are bound by Zld alone (Zld-only).
claims.source: For the Opa 3 hr and Zld nc13-14 comparison, these datasets have 6087 peaks in common (Opa-Zld overlap), whereas 9998 regions were bound by Opa alone (Opa-only) and 10781 regions were bound by Zld alone (Zld-only) (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A Venn diagram.

claims.claim: 16% of Opa-only peaks contain at least one Opa motif.
claims.source: As expected, the top motifs in each class matched the Opa or Zld consensus sequences with 16% of the Opa-only peaks containing at least one Opa motif; 55% of the Zld-only peaks containing at least one Zld motif; and 5% and 15% of the Opa-Zld overlap peaks containing at least one Opa or one Zld motif, respectively (Figure 2B–D; see also Figure 2—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing motif enrichment analysis.

claims.claim: 55% of Zld-only peaks contain at least one Zld motif.
claims.source: As expected, the top motifs in each class matched the Opa or Zld consensus sequences with 16% of the Opa-only peaks containing at least one Opa motif; 55% of the Zld-only peaks containing at least one Zld motif; and 5% and 15% of the Opa-Zld overlap peaks containing at least one Opa or one Zld motif, respectively (Figure 2B–D; see also Figure 2—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing motif enrichment analysis.

claims.claim: The second-most significant motif identified in Opa-only peaks corresponds to Dref (6%).
claims.source: The second-most significant motif identified in each class of called peaks corresponds to Dref (6%) for Opa-only; Caudal (Cad; 14%) for Zld-only; and Trl/GAF (11%) for Opa-Zld overlap (Figure 2B–D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B-D.

claims.claim: The second-most significant motif identified in Zld-only peaks corresponds to Caudal (Cad; 14%).
claims.source: The second-most significant motif identified in each class of called peaks corresponds to Dref (6%) for Opa-only; Caudal (Cad; 14%) for Zld-only; and Trl/GAF (11%) for Opa-Zld overlap (Figure 2B–D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B-D.

claims.claim: The second-most significant motif identified in Opa-Zld overlap peaks corresponds to Trl/GAF (11%).
claims.source: The second-most significant motif identified in each class of called peaks corresponds to Dref (6%) for Opa-only; Caudal (Cad; 14%) for Zld-only; and Trl/GAF (11%) for Opa-Zld overlap (Figure 2B–D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B-D.

claims.claim: Dref is a BED finger-type transcription factor shown to bind to the sequence 5′-TATCGATA, a highly conserved sequence in the core promoters of many Drosophila genes.
claims.source: Dref (DNA replication-related element-binding factor) is a BED finger-type transcription factor shown to bind to the sequence 5′-TATCGATA (Hirose et al., 1993), a highly conserved sequence in the core promoters of many Drosophila genes (Ohler et al., 2002), whereas Cad encodes a homeobox transcription factor that is maternally provided and forms a concentration-gradient enriched at the posterior (Mlodzik et al., 1985).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Cad encodes a homeobox transcription factor that is maternally provided and forms a concentration-gradient enriched at the posterior.
claims.source: Dref (DNA replication-related element-binding factor) is a BED finger-type transcription factor shown to bind to the sequence 5′-TATCGATA (Hirose et al., 1993), a highly conserved sequence in the core promoters of many Drosophila genes (Ohler et al., 2002), whereas Cad encodes a homeobox transcription factor that is maternally provided and forms a concentration-gradient enriched at the posterior (Mlodzik et al., 1985).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Cad exhibits preferential activation of DPE-containing promoters.
claims.source: Cad exhibits preferential activation of DPE-containing promoters (Shir-Shapira et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Trl/GAF is a transcriptional factor that regulates chromatin structure by promoting the open chromatin conformation in promoter gene regions, with optimal binding to the pentamer 5'-GAGAG-3'.
claims.source: Trl/GAF is a transcriptional factor that regulates chromatin structure by promoting the open chromatin conformation in promoter gene regions, with optimal binding to the pentamer 5'-GAGAG-3' (Chopra et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa and Zld can bind to the same enhancers as well as independently to distinct enhancers.
claims.source: Furthermore, a direct comparison of the Opa (3 hr) and Zld ChIP-seq occupancy at nc13-14, through aggregation plots, suggests that these two transcription factors can bind to the same enhancers (e.g. Figure 2G) as well as independently, to distinct enhancers (e.g. Figure 2E,F).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by aggregation plots in Figure 2E-G.

claims.claim: The respective Opa and Zld binding sites appear explanatory for the observed in vivo occupancy to DNA sequences as the matches to the consensus sequences correlate with the center of the peak.
claims.source: Indeed, the respective sites appear explanatory for the observed in vivo occupancy to DNA sequences as the matches to the consensus sequences correlate with the center of the peak (Figure 2E–G).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by aggregation plots in Figure 2E-G.

claims.claim: Protein levels of Opa are greatly diminished upon opa short hairpin (sh) RNAi (sh_opa).
claims.source: Using an anti-Opa antibody, we confirmed that protein levels are greatly diminished upon opa short hairpin (sh) RNAi (sh_opa) but are retained, though slightly reduced in sh_zld (Figure 3A; ~1.4 fold reduction, see Materials and methods).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Opa protein levels are retained, though slightly reduced (~1.4 fold reduction) in sh_zld.
claims.source: Using an anti-Opa antibody, we confirmed that protein levels are greatly diminished upon opa short hairpin (sh) RNAi (sh_opa) but are retained, though slightly reduced in sh_zld (Figure 3A; ~1.4 fold reduction, see Materials and methods).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: opa expression is only partially under Zld regulation.
claims.source: This result suggests that opa expression is only partially under Zld regulation, and indicates these factors may have separable roles.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the observation that Opa levels are only slightly reduced in sh_zld.

claims.claim: Expression phenotypes for sog and en are similar in opa1 mutants and sh_opa embryos.
claims.source: We also compared gene expression between opa1 mutants (Benedyk et al., 1994; Cimbora and Sakonju, 1995) and sh_opa embryos by performing in situ hybridization to visualize transcripts of representative Opa target genes sog and engrailed (en) (see Figure 1 and Clark and Akam, 2016; Benedyk et al., 1994). We found that expression phenotypes for sog and en were similar in these two opa mutant genotypes (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Over 667 genes were found to be significantly downregulated (adjusted p value<0.05) in sh_opa embryos at nc14D.
claims.source: Specifically, RNA-seq data support the view that Opa regulates zygotic expression of genes broadly in embryos at nc14 (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1F); over 667 genes were found to be significantly downregulated (adjusted p value<0.05; Figure 3—source data 1) and 36.8% are Opa-only bound targets (Figure 3—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing RNA-seq analysis.

claims.claim: 36.8% of downregulated genes in sh_opa embryos are Opa-only bound targets.
claims.source: Specifically, RNA-seq data support the view that Opa regulates zygotic expression of genes broadly in embryos at nc14 (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1F); over 667 genes were found to be significantly downregulated (adjusted p value<0.05; Figure 3—source data 1) and 36.8% are Opa-only bound targets (Figure 3—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing RNA-seq analysis.

claims.claim: 350 genes were significantly upregulated (adjusted p value<0.05) upon opa knockdown.
claims.source: Surprisingly, despite Opa's canonical role as an activator, we also found that 350 genes were significantly upregulated upon opa knockdown (adjusted p value<0.05; Figure 3—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing RNA-seq analysis.

claims.claim: Affected genes in sh_opa embryos exhibit a wide variety of patterns that span both the DV and AP axes, including terminal regions, in both up- and down-regulated classes.
claims.source: Using the DVEX database of spatial transcript expression patterns inferred from single-cell sequencing of the stage six embryo (just following the late nc14D timepoint analyzed by our RNA-seq analysis) (Karaiskos et al., 2017), we found that affected genes in sh_opa embryos exhibit a wide variety of patterns that span both the DV and AP axes, including terminal regions, in both up- and down-regulated classes (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: The genes doc2 and doc3 expressed in the presumptive dorsal ectoderm are significantly upregulated in sh_opa embryos.
claims.source: In particular, the genes doc2 and doc3 expressed in the presumptive dorsal ectoderm at this stage (Reim et al., 2003) are significantly upregulated in sh_opa embryos (Figure 3D and Figure 3—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work on doc2/doc3 expression.

claims.claim: opa mutants exhibit a u-shaped/tailup cuticular phenotype, typically relating to problems with dorsal ectoderm patterning and germ band retraction.
claims.source: We noticed that opa mutants also exhibit a u-shaped/tailup cuticular phenotype (weak relative to strong pair-rule phenotype; Jürgens et al., 1984; Benedyk et al., 1994), typically relating to problems with dorsal ectoderm patterning and, later, germ band retraction (e.g. Reim et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa (3 hr) ChIP-seq peaks were identified in promoter-proximal regions [transcription start site (TSS) ±3 kb] of both up- and down-regulated genes.
claims.source: To determine if observed changes in expression relate to direct action of Opa, we assessed whether Opa binding was associated with affected genes. Opa (3 hr) ChIP-seq peaks were identified in promoter-proximal regions [transcription start site (TSS) ±3 kb] of both up- and down-regulated genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Some regions with Opa binding were also co-occupied by Zld later at cellularization, but more so for the upregulated gene set.
claims.source: Some of these regions were also co-occupied by Zld later at cellularization, but more so for the upregulated gene set (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C, F).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C, F.

claims.claim: Upregulated genes in sh_opa embryos tend to relate to nervous system development/neurogenesis.
claims.source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis for these two sets of genes also demonstrate that upregulated genes tend to relate to nervous system development/neurogenesis; whereas downregulated genes tend to relate to cellular processes such as biogenesis of organelles and metabolism (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: Downregulated genes in sh_opa embryos tend to relate to cellular processes such as biogenesis of organelles and metabolism.
claims.source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis for these two sets of genes also demonstrate that upregulated genes tend to relate to nervous system development/neurogenesis; whereas downregulated genes tend to relate to cellular processes such as biogenesis of organelles and metabolism (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Opa is associated with genes expressed along both the anterior-posterior (AP) and dorsal-ventral (DV) axes.
claims.source: Within the total set of 16085 Opa ChIP peaks observed at the 3 hr timepoint we found, surprisingly, that Opa is associated with genes expressed along both the anterior-posterior (AP; Figure 4A–B', D–E') and dorsal-ventral (DV; Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) axes.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: Opa binding at the 3 hr timepoint is associated with enhancers that are initiated in nc14.
claims.source: We also found evidence in occupancy trends for Opa and Zld that suggest both these factors influence the timing of enhancer action. Opa binding at the 3 hr timepoint is associated with enhancers that are initiated in nc14: hb_stripe (Figure 4A'; Koromila and Stathopoulos, 2017; Perry et al., 2012), slp1_DESE (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C; Prazak et al., 2010), and oc_Prox (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B; Chen et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and references to figures.

claims.claim: Zld binding during nc13-14 and nc14 late is associated primarily with enhancers active earlier such as the hb_stripe enhancer.
claims.source: In contrast, Zld binding during the same stage, encompassed by Zld nc13-14 and nc14 late ChIP-seq, is associated primarily with enhancers active earlier such as the hb_stripe enhancer, whereas the hb_HG4-7 enhancer active later is not bound by Zld though it is associated with Opa (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Late-acting enhancers (eve_LE and rho_SHA) are bound predominantly by Opa.
claims.source: Similarly at the even skipped (eve) and rhomboid (rho) loci, late-acting enhancers (i.e. eve_LE and rho_SHA) are bound predominantly by Opa; whereas, enhancers active earlier (i.e. eve3/7, rho_NEE or oc_Distal) receive input from Opa and Zld or Zld only (Figure 4B,B' and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B, B' and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, D.

claims.claim: Opa is preferentially associated with promoters, whether or not Zld is co-associated.
claims.source: Furthermore, we found evidence that Opa is preferentially associated with promoters, whether or not Zld is co-associated (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A) as demonstrated by calculating the distances of ChIP-seq peak centers to TSS for both the Opa (3 hr) and (4 hr) samples (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, B.

claims.claim: Binding of Zld to Zld-only enhancers occurs in more distal regions at stage 5 (nc13/14 and nc14 late samples).
claims.source: While Zld was shown to preferentially associate with promoters at a much earlier stage (nc8; Harrison et al., 2011), we found that binding of Zld to Zld-only enhancers occurs in more distal regions at stage 5 (i.e. nc13/14 and nc14 late samples) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Zld-only bound regions are depleted for H3K4me3 as well as for H3K4me1 at both nc14A and nc14C timepoints relative to Opa-only or Opa-Zld overlap bound regions.
claims.source: Our analysis shows that Zld-only bound regions are depleted for H3K4me3, as shown previously (X.-Y. Li et al., 2014), as well as for H3K4me1 at both time points relative to Opa-only or Opa-Zld overlap bound regions (Figure 4F,G).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and shown in Figure 4F, G.

claims.claim: A general decrease in chromatin accessibility was associated with the sh_opa sample relative to wt in nc14D embryos.
claims.source: A general decrease in chromatin accessibility was associated with the sh_opa sample relative to wt in nc14D embryos (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: Opa-Zld overlap regions had, on average, ~2 fold higher ATAC-seq signal (accessibility) in wt than those bound solely by either Zld or Opa.
claims.source: Of the Opa-bound ChIP-seq defined peak regions, those also occupied by Zld (i.e. Opa-Zld overlap regions) had, on average, ~2 fold higher ATAC-seq signal (i.e. accessibility) in wt than those bound solely by either Zld or Opa (i.e. Zld-only or Opa-only) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: opa RNAi (sh_opa) decreases accessibility at Opa-only regions but also at the Opa-Zld overlap bound regions.
claims.source: opa RNAi (sh_opa) decreases accessibility at Opa-only regions but also at the Opa-Zld overlap bound regions (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Occupancy of both Opa and Zld is a better indicator of open chromatin regions than either factor alone.
claims.source: In summary, occupancy of both Opa and Zld is a better indicator of open chromatin regions than either factor alone; and, surprisingly, Opa regulates chromatin accessibility at Opa-only as well as Zld-co-bound regions.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of ATAC-seq findings.

claims.claim: Opa regulates chromatin accessibility at Opa-only as well as Zld-co-bound regions.
claims.source: In summary, occupancy of both Opa and Zld is a better indicator of open chromatin regions than either factor alone; and, surprisingly, Opa regulates chromatin accessibility at Opa-only as well as Zld-co-bound regions.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of ATAC-seq findings.

claims.claim: Single embryos of stage nc14B that ectopically express opa (UAS-opa) exhibit a clear increase in chromatin accessibility across Opa-bound regions.
claims.source: To do this, we ectopically-expressed full-length opa again using the maternal-zygotic MTD-Gal4 driver to ensure strong early embryonic expression. Single embryos of stage nc14B that ectopically express opa (UAS-opa) in this fashion exhibit a clear increase in chromatin accessibility across Opa-bound regions (Figure 5A) suggesting that Opa acts to open chromatin.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: All Opa-bound regions - both Opa/Zld overlap and Opa only regions - are not affected upon zld knock-down (sh_zld).
claims.source: However, all Opa-bound regions - both Opa/Zld overlap and Opa only regions - are not affected upon zld knock-down (sh_zld) (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-C, E-G), whereas Zld only regions are decreased in accessibility but only at an earlier timepoint, nc13, not at nc14 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3H compare with 3D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Zld only regions are decreased in accessibility upon zld knock-down but only at an earlier timepoint, nc13, not at nc14.
claims.source: However, all Opa-bound regions - both Opa/Zld overlap and Opa only regions - are not affected upon zld knock-down (sh_zld) (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-C, E-G), whereas Zld only regions are decreased in accessibility but only at an earlier timepoint, nc13, not at nc14 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3H compare with 3D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Opa, not Zld, regulates chromatin accessibility at nc14.
claims.source: While our results demonstrate that Opa, not Zld, regulates chromatin accessibility at nc14, we cannot exclude an accessory role for Zld.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the ATAC-seq data comparing sh_opa and sh_zld.

claims.claim: Ectopic expression of opa results in a trend toward shift in the positions of nucleosomes relative to binding sites.
claims.source: Ectopic expression of opa results in a trend toward shift in the positions of nucleosomes relative to binding sites (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G, H), suggesting that Opa displaces nucleosomes.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1G, H.

claims.claim: There is a shift to larger motif-nucleosome distance upon ectopic expression of opa compared to wildtype.
claims.source: We observe a shift to larger motif-nucleosome distance upon ectopic expression of opa compared to wildtype (Figure 5E,F; red versus blue lines, respectively). These data support the view that Opa occupancy on DNA displaces nucleosomes.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5E, F.

claims.claim: Opa occupancy on DNA displaces nucleosomes.
claims.source: We observe a shift to larger motif-nucleosome distance upon ectopic expression of opa compared to wildtype (Figure 5E,F; red versus blue lines, respectively). These data support the view that Opa occupancy on DNA displaces nucleosomes.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the nucleosome positioning analysis.

claims.claim: In opa mutant embryos there is a shift to smaller motif-nucleosome distance, which supports the view that Opa is required to displace nucleosomes.
claims.source: A recent study found that alternatively in opa mutant embryos there is a shift to smaller distance, which also supports the view that Opa is required to displace nucleosomes (Soluri et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to a recent study.

claims.claim: There is 88.5% overlap (3301 peaks) between the opa1 and sh_opa closed chromatin peaks.
claims.source: Chromatin accessibility as characterized by single-embryo ATAC-seq revealed 88.5% overlap between the opa1 and sh_opa closed chromatin peaks (versus open peaks in control), as well as 75% overlap between the sh_opa closed (accessible/open peaks in control) and UAS-opa open peaks (non-accessible/closed peaks in control) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: There is 75% overlap (3187 peaks) between the sh_opa closed and UAS-opa open peaks.
claims.source: Chromatin accessibility as characterized by single-embryo ATAC-seq revealed 88.5% overlap between the opa1 and sh_opa closed chromatin peaks (versus open peaks in control), as well as 75% overlap between the sh_opa closed (accessible/open peaks in control) and UAS-opa open peaks (non-accessible/closed peaks in control) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The VT15161 en enhancer exhibits an increase in accessibility in response to higher Opa levels, but a decrease in both sh_opa and opa1 mutants.
claims.source: For example, the VT15161 en enhancer (Kvon et al., 2014) exhibits an increase in accessibility in response to higher Opa levels, but a decrease in both sh_opa and opa1 mutants (Figure 5C, blue shaded region).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Similar Opa-dependent accessibility trends were identified for oc_Proximal, sog_Distal, and hb_stripe enhancers.
claims.source: Similar trends were identified for oc_Proximal, sog_Distal, and hb_stripe enhancers (Figure 5D,G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E; blue shaded regions) (Perry et al., 2011; Koromila and Stathopoulos, 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and shown in Figure 5D, G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: The accessibility of en, oc_Proximal, sog_Distal, and hb_stripe enhancers was not affected in sh_zld.
claims.source: Moreover, the accessibility of these same enhancers was not affected in sh_zld (e.g. Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, E, F).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, E, F.

claims.claim: Accessibility at eve_3–7 enhancer was affected by changes in both opa and zld.
claims.source: On the other hand, accessibility at other enhancer sequences, such as eve_3–7, was affected by changes in both opa and zld (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C; grey-shaded box).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Opa-bound regions fall into three classes: (i) regions that require Opa for accessibility; (ii) regions that require both Opa and Zld for accessibility; and (iii) regions that require Zld, but not Opa, for accessibility.
claims.source: The Opa-bound regions fall into three classes: (i) regions that require Opa for accessibility (blue-shaded regions); (ii) regions that require both Opa and Zld for accessibility (grey-shaded regions); and (iii) regions that require Zld, but not Opa, for accessibility [mint-shaded regions; e.g. enhancer sog_intronic (Markstein et al., 2002) and eve_LE (Fujioka et al., 2013; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C)].
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and references to figures.

claims.claim: Not all regions that are bound by Opa require this factor for accessibility.
claims.source: Collectively, these results support the view that Opa can influence chromatin accessibility, but not all regions that are bound by Opa require this factor for accessibility (i.e. class iii).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the ATAC-seq data.

claims.claim: At Opa-Zld overlap regions, in which both factors are bound, either Opa or Zld can suffice to support accessibility.
claims.source: It is possible that at Opa-Zld overlap regions, in which both factors are bound, either Opa or Zld can suffice to support accessibility.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a speculation based on the ATAC-seq data.

claims.claim: zld mutant embryos exhibit loss of expression for hb, sna, and sog at nc13.
claims.source: Even early, at nc13, zld mutant embryos exhibit loss of expression for all three genes examined (hb, sna, and sog), supporting the view that Zld is necessary for early gene expression (Figure 6C,E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6C, E.

claims.claim: Little difference in expression of hb, sna, and sog was observed in opa mutants at nc13.
claims.source: In contrast, little difference in expression was observed in opa mutants at nc13. This is unsurprising as opa is not expressed at nc13 and therefore would not be expected to affect patterning at this stage (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: At nc14C, opa mutants exhibit expression defects, as both sog and hb expression is diminished.
claims.source: Later, at nc14C, opa mutants do exhibit expression defects, as both sog and hb expression is diminished (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Expression defects in opa mutants at nc14C likely relate to lack of Opa input at sog_Distal, hb_stripe, and hb_HG4-7 enhancers that exhibit Opa-dependent changes in accessibility.
claims.source: These expression defects likely relate to lack of Opa input at sog_Distal, hb_stripe, and hb_HG4-7 enhancers that exhibit Opa-dependent changes in accessibility (Figure 5G; Figure 4A,A').
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation linking expression defects to accessibility changes.

claims.claim: ATAC-seq data for nc14B individual embryos in which opa was ectopically expressed (UAS-opa) exhibit a significant increase in chromatin accessibility at regions bound by Opa early (ChIP-seq 3 hr).
claims.source: In addition to these findings relating to patterning, we also observe temporal bias in Opa's genomic effects. ATAC-seq data for nc14B individual embryos in which opa was ectopically expressed (UAS-opa) exhibit a significant increase in chromatin accessibility at regions bound by Opa early (ChIP-seq 3 hr; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-C.

claims.claim: Ectopic expression of opa failed to increase accessibility at late-only regions bound by Opa (ChIP-seq 4 hr peaks not also present early) when assayed at nc14B.
claims.source: However, ectopic expression of opa failed to increase accessibility at late-only regions bound by Opa (ChIP-seq 4 hr peaks not also present early) when assayed at nc14B (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, D.

claims.claim: Only ChIP-seq regions that were present at the early timepoint (3 hr peaks as well as 3 hr + 4 hr overlap peaks) exhibited decreased accessibility upon opa RNAi.
claims.source: Furthermore, only ChIP-seq regions that were present at the early timepoint exhibited decreased accessibility upon opa RNAi (i.e. 3 hr peaks as well as 3 hr + 4 hr overlap peaks). These data further support the view that Opa binding is dynamic and associated with changes in accessibility.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the ATAC-seq data.

claims.claim: Opa-dependent changes in chromatin accessibility occur near genes that are downregulated as well as those that are upregulated upon sh_opa.
claims.source: Finally, to provide additional insight into Opa's function, we examined how Opa-dependent changes in chromatin accessibility correlate with changes in gene expression. Opa ATAC-seq peak regions were associated with the nearest gene transcription start site (TSS) to calculate overlap gene counts with opa mutant RNA-seq up- and down-regulated genes for nc14D embryos. Surprisingly, we found that Opa-dependent changes in chromatin accessibility occur near genes that are downregulated as well as those that are upregulated upon sh_opa (Figure 6A,B; see Discussion).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6A, B.

claims.claim: Opa is a late-acting timing factor, and likely pioneer factor, which regulates gene expression throughout the embryo, along DV as well as AP axes.
claims.source: In summary, our experiments indicate that Opa is a late-acting timing factor, and likely pioneer factor, which regulates gene expression throughout the embryo, along DV as well as AP axes.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the main findings.

claims.claim: opa mutants exhibit broad DV patterning changes in addition to previously identified AP patterning phenotypes.
claims.source: We show that opa mutants exhibit broad DV patterning changes in addition to previously identified AP patterning phenotypes and its role as a broadly-acting regulator of gene expression is supported by whole-genome gene expression profiling of sh_opa mutant embryos by RNA-seq.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing findings from RNA-seq and in situ hybridization.

claims.claim: Opa likely acts directly to regulate gene expression, as Opa chromatin immunoprecipitation demonstrates widespread binding throughout the genome.
claims.source: Opa likely acts directly to regulate gene expression, as Opa chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) demonstrates widespread binding throughout the genome, including at the sog_Distal enhancer.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing ChIP-seq findings.

claims.claim: opa knockdown affects chromatin accessibility at regions occupied by Opa but not by Zld.
claims.source: Additional data from single-embryo ATAC-seq provide insight into the mechanism by which Opa supports gene expression as opa knockdown affects chromatin accessibility at regions occupied by Opa but not by Zld, as determined by ChIP analysis.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing ATAC-seq findings.

claims.claim: Chromatin accessibility in early embryos appears to be predominantly supported by Zld and then, once Opa is expressed in mid-nc14, the two factors seem to work together in this role.
claims.source: Chromatin accessibility in early embryos appears to be predominantly supported by Zld and then, once Opa is expressed in mid-nc14, the two factors seem to work together in this role.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the combined ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq data.

claims.claim: Zygotic genes (or particular enhancers) associated with mid-nc14 to gastrulation or later appear to be preferentially bound by Opa.
claims.source: However, zygotic genes (or particular enhancers) associated with mid-nc14 to gastrulation or later, appear to be preferentially bound by Opa.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of ChIP-seq data showing Opa binding at late-acting enhancers.

claims.claim: Opa acts following the pioneer factor Zld to influence timing of zygotic gene activation at the whole-genome level by actively increasing late-acting enhancer accessibility.
claims.source: Therefore, we suggest that Opa acts following the pioneer factor Zld to influence timing of zygotic gene activation at the whole-genome level by actively increasing late-acting enhancer accessibility (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as the main conclusion and shown in Figure 6E model.

claims.claim: Opa-bound regions (with and without Zelda) are enriched for late histone methylation.
claims.source: Furthermore, Opa-bound regions (with and without Zelda) are enriched for late histone methylation, and this may relate either to Opa's preference promoters or suggest a more causative function for Opa with respect to chromatin state.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the histone mark analysis.

claims.claim: Opa's regulatory impacts during development may include both control of epigenetic marks as well as chromatin accessibility at promoters and/or promoter-proximal cis-regulatory elements.
claims.source: Opa's regulatory impacts during development may therefore include both control of epigenetic marks as well as chromatin accessibility at promoters and/or promoter-proximal cis-regulatory elements.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation about Opa's mechanism of action.

claims.claim: Opa presumably influences the activity of other transcription factors such as Run when co-bound to enhancers through mechanisms that are as yet not completely understood.
claims.source: Further, in addition to supporting gene expression in a general manner by making chromatin accessible, Opa also presumably influences the activity of other transcription factors such as Run when co-bound to enhancers through mechanisms that are as yet not completely understood (Koromila and Stathopoulos, 2019; Prazak et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Dref is highly enriched at promoters and has been implicated in multiple roles during Drosophila development including regulation of expression of signaling pathway components and chromatin organization including insulator and chromatin remodeling functions.
claims.source: For example, a motif matching the Dref binding consensus is enriched at Opa ChIP-seq peaks. Dref is highly enriched at promoters and has been implicated in multiple roles during Drosophila development including regulation of expression of signaling pathway components and chromatin organization including insulator and chromatin remodeling functions (rev. in Tue et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to a review article.

claims.claim: Dref has been linked to insulator function.
claims.source: In particular, as Dref has been linked to insulator function (Gurudatta et al., 2013) and Zld has been shown to be associated with locus-specific TAD boundary insulation (Hug et al., 2017), future studies should examine whether temporal progression of gene regulatory networks is supported not only by the sequential action of pioneer factors to affect chromatin accessibility at enhancer/promoters but also by influencing chromatin conformation.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Zld has been shown to be associated with locus-specific TAD boundary insulation.
claims.source: In particular, as Dref has been linked to insulator function (Gurudatta et al., 2013) and Zld has been shown to be associated with locus-specific TAD boundary insulation (Hug et al., 2017), future studies should examine whether temporal progression of gene regulatory networks is supported not only by the sequential action of pioneer factors to affect chromatin accessibility at enhancer/promoters but also by influencing chromatin conformation.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Regions of chromatin accessibility are thought to be established sequentially, where enhancers are opened in advance of promoters and insulators.
claims.source: Regions of chromatin accessibility are thought to be established sequentially, where enhancers are opened in advance of promoters and insulators (Blythe and Wieschaus, 2016a) and our results show enrichment of Opa binding near promoters.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa may influence gene expression timing by affecting accessibility at promoters, possibly in combination with Dref.
claims.source: Opa may therefore influence gene expression timing by affecting accessibility at promoters, possibly, in combination with Dref.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation based on Opa's promoter enrichment and Dref motif enrichment.

claims.claim: Trl/GAF and Dref were shown to be associated with early versus late embryonic expression (stage five and later), respectively.
claims.source: Furthermore, Trl/GAF and Dref were shown to be associated with early versus late embryonic expression (stage five and later), respectively (Darbo et al., 2013; Schulz et al., 2015; Hochheimer et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa, like Dref, is a late-acting factor, and Trl/GAF may work early with Zelda.
claims.source: These results collectively support the view that Opa, like Dref, is a late-acting factor, and that Trl/GAF may work early with Zelda.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the motif enrichment data.

claims.claim: Trl/GAF acts coordinately but separately from Zld to support chromatin accessibility in regions that do not require Zld.
claims.source: However, other studies have shown that Trl/GAF acts coordinately but separately from Zld to support chromatin accessibility in regions that do not require Zld (Moshe and Kaplan, 2017).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: The triggering of temporal waves of gene regulation in response to chromatin accessibility changes is a potentially widespread mechanism used to control developmental progression.
claims.source: More generally, the triggering of temporal waves of gene regulation in response to chromatin accessibility changes is a potentially widespread mechanism used to control developmental progression.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a broader implication of the findings.

claims.claim: The opa transcript is over 17 kB in length, and this relatively long transcript size may contribute to its expression in late nc14.
claims.source: To start, the opa transcript is over 17 kB in length, and this relatively long transcript size may contribute to its expression in late nc14 as previously studies have suggested that transcripts of this length are difficult (or impossible) to transcribe in earlier nuclear cycles due to short interphase length (i.e. nc13, etc) (Sandler et al., 2018; Shermoen and O'Farrell, 1991).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to prior work on transcript length and timing.

claims.claim: opa expression is regulated by the nuclear-cytoplasmic (N/C) ratio.
claims.source: opa expression is also regulated by the nuclear-cytoplasmic (N/C) ratio, whereas other genes like snail are not sensitive to N/C ratio but appear instead to be regulated by a maternal clock (Lu et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: As a N/C-ratio responsive gene, opa expression may be regulated by maternal repression.
claims.source: It has been hypothesized that the initiation of N/C ratio-responsive genes is regulated by a maternal repressor, the activity of which is counteracted by increasing N/C ratio possibly through dilution (e.g. Hamm and Harrison, 2018). Therefore, as a N/C-ratio responsive gene, opa expression may be regulated by maternal repression.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to prior work, as a speculation about opa regulation.

claims.claim: Genes of different timing classes may be preferentially regulated by different pioneer factors, and multiple factors may act coordinately to control stage-specific gene expression.
claims.source: We propose that genes of different timing classes may be preferentially regulated by different pioneer factors, and that multiple factors may act coordinately to control stage-specific gene expression.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a proposal based on the findings.

claims.claim: At nc14, which encompasses the MBT, Opa appears to be one timing factor acting, but Zld and possibly also other factors support this process.
claims.source: For example, at nc14, which encompasses the MBT, Opa appears to be one timing factor acting, but Zld and possibly also other factors support this process.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claims.claim: No gross cellularization defects or changes in length of the cell cycle were detected in sh_opa embryos despite significant expression changes in important regulators of this process such as Z600/frühstart (frs).
claims.source: Despite significant expression changes in important regulators of this process such as Z600/frühstart (frs; Grosshans et al., 2003) in sh_opa embryos, no gross cellularization defects or changes in length of the cell cycle were detected.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to prior work on frs.

claims.claim: Late Z600/frs expression at nc14D is associated with the dorsal ectoderm, and loss of Opa may present defects at later stages possibly in relation to function of dorsal tissues such as amnioserosa.
claims.source: However, late Z600/frs expression at nc14D is associated with the dorsal ectoderm (see Figure 2C in; Grosshans et al., 2003), and loss of Opa may present defects at later stages possibly in relation to function of dorsal tissues such as amnioserosa.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to prior work, as a speculation.

claims.claim: Zld regulates expression of Z600/frs as well as a number of other genes involved in cellularization such as slam, halo, btsz, bnk, nullo, CG14427, and Sry-α.
claims.source: In addition, Zld regulates expression of Z600/frs as well as a number of other genes involved in cellularization such as slam, halo, btsz, bnk, nullo, CG14427, and Sry-α (Nien et al., 2011; Lu et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa regulates expression of Z600/frs, slam, halo, and bnk.
claims.source: Of these genes, we also found evidence that Opa regulates expression not only of Z600/frs but also slam, halo, and bnk (see Figure 3—source data 1: RNA-seq data).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion referencing RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: Opa sits at the top of a gene regulatory hierarchy that facilitates levels of expression of genes involved in MBT as well as other N/C-ratio sensing genes including sog and odd-skipped/CG3851.
claims.source: As opa expression is dependent on the ratio of nuclear to cytoplasmic volume (N/C-ratio sensing) (Lu et al., 2009), our data support the view that Opa sits at the top of a gene regulatory hierarchy that facilitates levels of expression of the genes above, which are involved in MBT, as well as other N/C-ratio sensing genes including sog and odd-skipped/CG3851 (this study; Lu et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to prior work and current study data.

claims.claim: Degradation of maternal transcripts, an important part of the MBT, is not N/C-ratio dependent and likely relates to a function of Zld not Opa.
claims.source: Contrastingly, degradation of maternal transcripts, also an important part of the MBT, is not N/C-ratio dependent and likely relates to a function of Zld (Liang et al., 2008) not Opa.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Opa may not be involved in cell cycle pause as associated with zld mutants, but may contribute to regulation of other cellular processes.
claims.source: It is possible that Opa supports expression of some but not all genes that regulate MBT. For example, Opa may not be involved in cell cycle pause as associated with zld mutants (Liang et al., 2008), but may contribute to regulation of other cellular processes.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to prior work, as a speculation.

claims.claim: GO analysis of genes downregulated in sh_opa mutants suggest that Opa regulates genes involved in biogenesis of cellular components, mitochondria and other organelles, metabolism, and vesicle organization.
claims.source: GO analysis of genes downregulated in sh_opa mutants suggest that Opa regulates genes involved in biogenesis of cellular components, mitochondria and other organelles, metabolism, and vesicle organization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion referencing GO analysis results.

claims.claim: Pioneer factors may exhibit spatially constrained functions.
claims.source: Furthermore, pioneer factors may exhibit spatially constrained functions.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a general statement about pioneer factors.

claims.claim: Opa's expression in the embryonic trunk, but exclusion from the termini, suggest that additional late-acting factors may serve a pioneer role at the embryonic termini.
claims.source: Opa's expression in the embryonic trunk, but exclusion from the termini, suggest that additional late-acting factors may serve a pioneer role at the embryonic termini.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation based on Opa's expression pattern.

claims.claim: The transcription factor Orthodenticle (Otd) functions in a feed-forward relay from Bicoid to support expression of genes at the anterior of embryos.
claims.source: For example, a recent study suggests that the transcription factor Orthodenticle (Otd) functions in a feed-forward relay from Bicoid to support expression of genes at the anterior of embryos (Datta et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to a recent study.

claims.claim: Cad is localized in a gradient that emanates from the posterior pole.
claims.source: Furthermore, our analysis of the Zld ChIP-seq dataset identified enrichment for Cad transcription factor binding motifs in Zld-bound regions. Cad is localized in a gradient that emanates from the posterior pole (Mlodzik et al., 1985).
